q: Is this a paid role?
a: This is a 100% volunteer role with no pay. Your time helps children learn directly in school hours.

q: What are the class timings?
a: Live classes happen only on weekdays between 8 AM and 3 PM, aligned with school hours.

q: Can I teach on weekends?
a: Core live sessions are weekday-only (8–15). If weekends are easier, we can explore a saturday first half or a tiny weekday slot (e.g., lunch 12:30–13:00).

q: What device do I need?
a: A tablet or laptop with stable internet works. A quiet space and headset helps too.

q: How much time do I need to commit?
a: Most volunteers give about 2 hours per week for at least 3 months to provide continuity for students.

q: What is this video about?
a: It’s a real class demo led by a volunteer, shared to give you a feel for how a SERVE session looks.

q: Do I need a separate call?
a: No separate call is needed. We’ll guide you step by step here on WhatsApp.

q: What is SERVE and how does it work?
a: SERVE connects volunteers to live classes in schools. You teach online while students join from their classroom with a local coordinator.

q: Is this a paid or volunteer role?
a: It is a 100% volunteer role with no pay.

q: How many hours per week are expected?
a: Most volunteers give about 2 hours per week, usually split across 2 short weekday sessions.

q: Are evening or weekend classes available?
a: Live classes are weekday-only between 8 AM and 3 PM to match school hours.

q: Do I need to teach every day?
a: No. Most volunteers teach 2 to 3 sessions per week.

q: What subjects and grades will I teach?
a: Most needs are for English, Math, or Science for grades 5 to 8, depending on the school.

q: Which language will I teach in?
a: We try to match you to a regional language so children can follow comfortably.

q: Can I teach only in English?
a: We try to prioritize a regional language whenever possible so students can follow easily.

q: Do I need prior teaching experience?
a: No. Many volunteers are first-time teachers. We guide you with simple tips and support.

q: Can I use a phone?
a: A tablet or laptop with stable internet is required. Phones are not recommended for teaching sessions.

q: How long does the program last?
a: We request a minimum commitment of about 3 months so children get continuity.

q: What if my schedule changes later?
a: That is okay. You can let us know and we will adjust or pause if needed.

q: Will I get a certificate?
a: Yes, a volunteer certificate is provided after completing the required sessions.

q: How are classes conducted?
a: Classes are conducted online while students join from their school’s smart classroom.

q: When do classes start after onboarding?
a: After onboarding, we match you to an open class based on your availability and language.

q: Who will support me if I face issues?
a: A local coordinator supports each class and helps you during sessions.
